title: Poweradmin: The email second factor is an mt_rand() six-digit code verified with no attempt limit or lockout, so an…
description: Poweradmin versions 4.0.0 through before 4.2.6, 4.3.0 through before 4.3.5, and 4.4.0 through before 4.4.1 use a six-digit email second factor code generated with PHP's mt_rand(), a non-cryptographically secure RNG, and do not limit the number of verification attempts. This allows an attacker who has the user's password to brute-force the second factor code within its validity window, defeating the purpose of MFA. Fixes addressing both the RNG and attempt limiting are available in versions 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1.
